_comment: WhatsApp inbound webhook (P8c). This block is the other half of the whatsapp block: the outbound side asks 'may I send this', this side answers 'did this really come from Meta, and what did it say'. Copy the 'whatsapp_webhook' block below into config/integrations.json, merged under the tenant key next to 'whatsapp'. The 'whatsapp' block it depends on already declares the contacts; this block adds no contact list of its own.
_note_secret: Configuration holds the NAME of an environment variable, never the value: app_secret_env and verify_token_env are references, so this file can be committed and reviewed. The Meta app secret is found in the Meta App Dashboard under Settings, Basic, App Secret. If the named variable is unset the block refuses rather than proceeding, because a webhook endpoint that verifies nothing accepts a message from anyone who knows the URL, and any agent holding whatsapp.send would then believe a customer wrote.
_note_verify_token: verify_token_env names the token Meta echoes during the one-time GET handshake (hub.mode=subscribe) when the webhook is first subscribed. It is a shared secret chosen by the operator, not issued by Meta, and it is compared in constant time. It is NOT the app secret and must not be the same value: the handshake is unauthenticated, so reusing the signing key there would expose it.
_note_no_http: This block ships no web server and no route. A framework is a dependency, a request object is a place for untrusted input to look structured, and every framework's 'I already parsed the body for you' convenience is the thing that breaks signature verification. A route does three lines of work - read the raw bytes, read the X-Hub-Signature-256 header, call the ingest function - and the function itself is testable without a socket.
_note_raw_bytes: The signature is computed over the exact bytes Meta sent. Parsing the body and re-serialising it can reorder keys or change whitespace and invalidate the signature, so the verification function takes bytes and never a dict.
_note_no_ingest_tool: There is deliberately no tool that accepts a webhook. A model able to call 'accept this webhook' could manufacture an inbound message, which would open a 24-hour service window for a customer who never wrote and lift the platform's own legal constraint. Ingest is called by the transport that has already verified Meta's signature; no agent reaches it.
_note_window: An accepted message records window_until, derived ONLY from Meta's own timestamp, never from our wall clock. A message whose timestamp is absent or unparsable reports window_until as null, meaning 'this message did not open the window', rather than opening a 24-hour window at the time our server happened to process the delivery. Note that the outbound path does not yet read this value: whatsapp.send checks the window against the operator's sheet register, so what this block records and what the outbound side reads are two sources. Closing that is a separate unit of work; it is recorded in BACKLOG.json rather than left implied.
_note_drops: Status callbacks (sent/delivered/read) and messages from numbers the operator never declared are DROPPED with a reason, not raised. Meta retries a non-2xx response, so a malformed or unrecognised delivery that raised would be redelivered forever. A refusal must be a decision, recorded, never an exception that produces a retry storm.
